messages.text:
"GAME DEVELOPMENT MASTER PROMPT

TITLE: THE LAST SANCTUARY

A CINEMATIC THIRD-PERSON SURVIVAL HORROR GAME

You are an expert AAA game development studio consisting of a game director, creative director, environment artist, character designer, 3D modeller, animator, gameplay programmer, AI programmer, level designer, sound designer, narrative writer and technical director.

Your task is to create an original, highly detailed, cinematic, immersive third-person survival-horror game titled:

THE LAST SANCTUARY

The game must have its own identity, characters, story, creatures, locations, visual design and gameplay mechanics.

Use the atmosphere, cinematic presentation, exploration, tension, puzzles and survival mechanics associated with premium survival-horror games as general inspiration. Do not copy any copyrighted characters, names, creatures, locations, maps, dialogue, music, logos or storylines from existing games.

This must feel like a professionally designed original game, not a basic zombie shooting demonstration.

==================================================

1. GAME IDENTITY AND CORE EXPERIENCE
   ==================================================

Game title: THE LAST SANCTUARY

Subtitle: THE DEVGHAR EXPERIMENT

Genre:

- Third-person survival horror.
- Action adventure.
- Exploration.
- Mystery and investigation.
- Resource management.
- Puzzle solving.
- Cinematic storytelling.

Platform priority:

- Android-compatible development where supported.
- PC-compatible architecture if the engine supports it.
- Adapt graphics and controls to the available hardware.

Camera:
Use an over-the-shoulder third-person camera.

The player should see the main character from behind, slightly over the right shoulder, with smooth camera movement and cinematic framing.

Allow camera adjustment and comfortable sensitivity settings.

The camera should:

- Follow the player naturally.
- Move smoothly while walking and running.
- Have appropriate movement during exploration.
- Allow aiming and inspection.
- Avoid clipping through walls.
- Provide cinematic camera transitions during important story scenes.

The overall experience must be mysterious, frightening, emotional and immersive.

==================================================
2. COMPLETE STORY AND GAME UNIVERSE

LOCATION:

The entire game takes place in Devgarh, a fictional isolated town in the Western Ghats of India.

Devgarh is surrounded by:

- Dense forests.
- Mountains.
- Abandoned roads.
- Waterfalls.
- Underground tunnels.
- Old government buildings.
- Colonial-era structures.
- Abandoned residential areas.

The town was once famous for its medical research centre.

In 1998, a secret organisation called AETHERIS BIOTECH began an underground biological research project.

The project was named PROJECT ECLIPSE.

Its objective was to develop a revolutionary biological treatment capable of repairing damaged human cells.

However, an experimental organism began changing living creatures in unpredictable ways.

The research facility was sealed.

The government classified the incident.

The town was evacuated.

Twenty-eight years later, mysterious radio signals begin transmitting from Devgarh.

The player discovers that the experiment was never completely shut down.

The research has continued underground.

And something is still alive.

==================================================
3. MAIN PLAYABLE CHARACTER

Character name: ARJUN RAO

Age: 29.

Nationality: Indian.

Profession: Former emergency-response officer.

Appearance:

- Realistic Indian male character.
- Medium athletic build.
- Natural facial proportions.
- Short black hair.
- Slight beard.
- Expressive eyes.
- Realistic skin texture.
- Detailed facial animation.
- Natural body proportions.

Clothing:

- Dark olive tactical jacket.
- Black inner shirt.
- Dark cargo trousers.
- Practical boots.
- Utility belt.
- Small shoulder bag.
- Wristwatch.

Do not make him look like a superhero.

His clothing should becom

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.
